audit.whatIsWrong: Cell Division is referred to eight times as 'his passive', 'his blob passive' or 'blob pickups', and the revive is never mentioned in either layer.
audit.why: Two separate mechanics live on that passive and the page only half-describes one. Every ability he lands sheds a blob he can walk over to heal — which is why 'step on blobs' is correct advice and why the entry should say the blobs come from HIS casts, not from damage taken. And on fatal damage he splits into four bloblets and revives if any survive, on a five-minute cooldown. A player who does not know the revive exists spends a 130-second Public Execution on a kill that does not happen. Five minutes is also long enough to be worth tracking, which makes it actionable rather than just a warning.
audit.corrected: Cell Division (P): every ability he lands sheds a blob he reabsorbs to heal, and on death he splits into four bloblets and revives if any survive — once every 5 minutes.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json — P Cell Division: 'Each time Zac hits an enemy with an ability, he sheds a chunk of himself that can be reabsorbed to restore Health... he will revive... This ability has a 5 minute cooldown.'
audits/top/zac__ambessa.json — mirror states the same 5 minute figure

audit.whatIsWrong: Unstable Matter is never named; it appears once as 'his W nuke'. Elastic Slingshot is the tracked matchup-defining ability and its cooldown is never given.
audit.why: Unstable Matter is percent-max-health MAGIC damage on a 5-second cooldown, which is the reason the late-game section is right that Ambessa 'bounces off' him — and it inverts the usual reading of a tank matchup, because every health item Zac buys makes his damage to her larger, and it is magic so armour does nothing about it. Elastic Slingshot is 21 seconds at rank 1, the longest engage cooldown Ambessa faces in this lane and the actual window the whole full layer keeps pointing at without a number.
audit.corrected: Unstable Matter (W), 5s, 350 range: percent-max-health magic damage. Elastic Slingshot (E), 21/18/15/12/9 — commit inside the 21s after he spends it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json — W Unstable Matter 'a percentage of their maximum health as magic damage', cd 5; E Elastic Slingshot cd 21/18/15/12/9

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings credit Ambessa with 'your passive armor-pen plus R's heal-on-damage' / 'your armor-pen passive plus R heal' (spikes[1].text, whys[4], mid). Stretching Strikes is also described only as a 'Q stretch-slow'.
audit.why: Public Execution grants no armour penetration and no healing in Riot's text — blink to the farthest champion in a chosen line, suppress, slam for damage and a stun. The kit file's 'heal' flag on her R is a tooltip-parsing misfire (see notes), and here it is propping up the claim that she shreds a tank, which is the reasoning a player would use to commit into a Zac she cannot actually kill through. Stretching Strikes is separately mis-described: it GRABS a target, and only becomes a throw-and-knockup if he then attacks a DIFFERENT enemy — so in lane he needs a minion to complete it, and denying him that second body denies the whole ability.
audit.corrected: Stretching Strikes (Q), 14/12.5/11/9.5/8, 800 range: a grab that only throws if he hits a second enemy. Public Execution has no armour pen and no heal.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json — Q Stretching Strikes 'grabbing an enemy. Attacking a different enemy will cause him to throw both targets towards each other'

audit.why: EVEN at 6/10 with Zac carry threat 7/10 fits 49.08% over 271 games. The already-audited Zac page rates the same lane the same way, and both content layers carry the identical win[] array stage-for-stage, so the two directions agree. No side or rating changed.

audit.why: The four spike moments are right: 4-5 is his sustain window, 6 is her first kill threat, first item is her peak, and late is his as he stacks health. I kept all four and replaced the mechanics — the level-6 card was justified by armour penetration and healing she does not have, and the late card by 'blob-sustained HP' when the real reason is Unstable Matter turning his own health purchases into damage against her.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json — W percentHealth, E cd 21 at rank 1

audit.whatIsWrong: The Repudiation brace is used correctly in wants.you[2] and spikes[2].text but the entry never states the general rule, and the blobs are treated as something to deny rather than something to time.
audit.why: Blobs are shed on every ability HE lands, so the densest blob field appears immediately after he commits a rotation — which is the same moment his Elastic Slingshot is on a 21-second timer. Stepping on blobs and committing are therefore the same window rather than two competing jobs, and the page currently presents them as separate chores.
audit.corrected: His rotation sheds the blobs AND spends the 21s Elastic Slingshot at the same time — walk the blobs on your way in, don't choose between them.
sources: champ-data/_kits/zac.json — P blob shed on ability hit, E cd 21/18/15/12/9

notes: MIRROR REUSED: audits/top/zac__ambessa.json was already written and I took the 5-minute Cell Division revive figure and the general shape of the lane from it rather than re-deriving them. Worth flagging for whoever applies these — that audit reports that the ZAC page's full layer is built around a fabricated Ambessa ability called 'Repeating Dashes' occupying 25 strings, and that zac.full.js phases[].side disagrees with its own content win[]. Neither problem exists on the Ambessa side: my two layers agree stage-for-stage with each other AND with zac's content win[], so applying my edits does not touch that conflict. KIT-FILE FLAG MISFIRES: champ-data/_kits/zac.json tags Elastic Slingshot with 'grounding', which Riot's text does not support — the parser caught 'attaches his arms to the ground'. I asserted no grounding. Its 'knockup' flag on the same ability is also unsupported by the description text, but the existing page already states the sling knock-up in two places and I neither added nor removed that claim. champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json separately tags Public Execution with 'heal' and W and R with 'grounding'; the derived 'armor-pen plus R heal' phrasing had leaked into three strings here and I removed it. WIN RATE: MC_WR_TABLES.ambessa.zac and the packet agree at 49.08 over 271 games.
